newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Placer Dome to exit from Marcopper. [CORRECTED 13:27 GMT 22/3]
newsitem.headline: Placer Dome to exit from Marcopper. [CORRECTED 13:27 GMT 22/3]

text.p: Placer Dome Inc said on Friday it was divesting its 39.9 percent stake in Marcopper Mining Corp to the mine's majority owner.
"Placer Dome has transferred to Marcopper Mining Corporation of the Philippines Placer Dome's 39.9 percent shareholding in the company," a statement issued by Placer Dome in Manila said.
Placer Dome will not receive any compensation for the shares it transfers to Marcopper. (Corrects from F Holdings)
Marcopper's majority owners are F Holdings, a private company controlled by the Bernadino family.
Marcopper's copper mine in Marinduque, 160 km (100 miles) south of Manila, has been closed since March last year when it suffered a major leak of tailings.

"We are withdrawing from Marcopper under an arrangement consistent with our values. This divestiture results from our lack of majority control of Marcopper, the differing priorities of the shareholder groups and the fact that Placer Dome no longer focuses on copper," the statement quoted Placer Dome chief executive John Willson as saying.
Willson said the move in no way affects Placer Dome's commitment to mitigate the effects of the tailings spill from the Marcopper mine into the Boac river.
The statement said Placer Dome continued to provide money to settle more than 2,000 claims for about 19 million pesos ($722,000) from people in 44 villages affected by the spill.
It said Placer Dome is continuing to clean up the river and less than 30 percent of the tailing remains on its banks.
It said the spill was not toxic and there was no immediate threat to human health.
Last year, Placer wrote off its investment in Marcopper and took a $43 million charge to earnings for the accident.
Two Placer executives at Marcopper face criminal charges for the spill.
